tier: free tier shape (new org, 2 vCPU / 2 GiB / 10 GB per sandbox); prepaid credit

free_tier.stated: unverified: the billing page says a new org starts at USD 0 and must add credits before creating a sandbox; a promo code adds credit, and a new org's free tier cap is 2 vCPU, 2 GiB RAM, 10 GB disk per sandbox and 4 vCPU, 8 GiB, 40 GB running at once. The home page advertises USD 10 free credit; the sign-up gate was not opened.
free_tier.notes: A promo code adds credit but the amount and availability are not published on the pages read. An OAuth public client can register anonymously, but that registration never creates a user or a session, so it grants no sandbox capacity. A sandbox account is created in the dashboard at https://www.platinum.dev/dashboard#signup.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a microVM, not a stored object; the free tier shape allows up to 10 GB disk per sandbox and 40 GB running at once for a new org

retention.stated: Sandboxes are persistent by default; auto_stop_minutes defaults to 0 (never), auto_archive_days to 7 and auto_delete_days to 0 (never). A stopped sandbox after 7 days is archived at the lower disk rate.
retention.notes: The 7-day default is the stopped-to-archive timer, not a deletion timer; auto_delete_days defaults to 0, so no automatic deletion is set.

egress.terms: Egress to public internet addresses is USD 0.04 per GiB; data a sandbox receives, preview URL traffic, sandbox-to-sandbox traffic and volume traffic do not count. Outbound traffic can be filtered per sandbox with allowOut and denyOut; a residential proxy is USD 8 per GiB in both directions and needs paid credit.

interface_detail: Cloud Hypervisor microVMs with a full Linux kernel, driven by TypeScript and Python SDKs, the pt CLI, a REST API at https://api.platinum.dev/v1, a hosted MCP server and an OpenAPI 3.1 specification. The Daytona SDK runs against Platinum unchanged and an E2B migration guide maps every SDK call.
tooling: npm install -g @platinum-dev/cli and the pt command, the @platinum-dev/sdk TypeScript and Python packages, the hosted MCP server, the Daytona SDK pointed at Platinum, and an SSH key injected into a sandbox.
chaining: A sandbox can hold a coding agent with its API key kept outside the VM and injected by the egress proxy for exact hosts, pause with memory and processes intact, fork into parallel rollouts, and expose a port under a signed preview URL.

limits.value: prepaid credit; new org starts at USD 0, credit packs USD 10, USD 50 or USD 200 and custom USD 5 to USD 1,000

free tier: 2 vCPU, 2 GiB RAM, 10 GB disk per sandbox; 4 vCPU, 8 GiB, 40 GB running at once; 10 templates. t2 after a verified email, a saved card and USD 25 paid: 8 vCPU, 16 GiB, 50 GB per sandbox; 128 vCPU, 256 GiB, 2,000 GB running at once
auto_stop_minutes 0 by default, auto_archive_days 7, auto_delete_days 0; a zero balance auto-stops running sandboxes after a 60-minute grace period
at balance zero, new compute create, start, resume, restore, clone and fork answer 402 insufficient_credits

limits_note: Compute is USD 0.0324 per vCPU-hour and USD 0.0108 per GiB-hour of RAM, billed per second while running; disk is USD 0.0526 per GB-month and USD 0.0263 archived. A month is 730 hours. Exposed ports are capped at 8 per sandbox and 32 per org per region, with 256 open connections per port and 64 from one address. Resource access tokens expire after 15 minutes.
binding_note: A new org starts at a USD 0 balance and a create needs prepaid credit, and its free shape is capped at 2 vCPU and 2 GiB per sandbox with 4 vCPU running at once; that gate and cap bind before the per-second rate or the 7-day archive timer.

identity_cost.detail: An account is created in the dashboard at https://www.platinum.dev/dashboard#signup; an API key is minted there or through pt login. A verified email and USD 5 paid reach t1, and a verified email, a saved card and USD 25 paid reach t2. The home page advertises USD 10 free credit; the sign-up form itself was not read, so the exact fields are unverified. OAuth public client registration is anonymous but never creates a user, session or access token.

reliability_note: Only running sandboxes bill compute; stopped sandboxes bill disk and are archived after 7 days by default. At a zero balance, running sandboxes get a 60-minute grace period and are then stopped, never deleted, and disks keep billing so the balance can stay negative. A stop can save only the disk, in which case the next start cold-boots and processes are gone; each stop reports memory_saved and each start reports restore.
confidence_note: Rates, egress, sandbox limits, timers, credit requirements and sign-up route are quoted from the first-party billing, sandboxes, quickstart, auth and docs pages read 2026-11-24. The advertised USD 10 free credit and the sign-up form fields are unverified because the dashboard is a login wall and the account step needs a sign-up.

notes: Platinum sells hardware-isolated Cloud Hypervisor microVM sandboxes for AI agents, billed per second while running. The unbundled rate is USD 0.0324 per vCPU-hour plus USD 0.0108 per GiB-hour of RAM, USD 0.108 an hour for 2 vCPU and 4 GiB; egress is USD 0.04 per GiB, paid from prepaid credit. A new org starts at a USD 0 balance and must add credit before it can create a sandbox, and its free shape is capped at 2 vCPU, 2 GiB and 10 GB per sandbox with 4 vCPU running at once, so credit and the free cap bind first. The home page advertises USD 10 free credit, but the sign-up form is behind a login wall and was not read; the exact credit and identity gate are unverified. An anonymous OAuth client registration grants no sandbox capacity. A self-hosted deployment of the control plane is documented separately and comes last behind this hosted offer.
